task: Explain a fictional association's garden-plot allocation process in about 80–120 words for applicants who assume the list is first-come, first-served. Describe priority and the draw in ordinary language without promising a plot or a waiting time. This is an explanation of the supplied local process, not of housing or public-allocation law.

facts.text: Vacant plots are first offered among applicants who do not already have an association plot.
A draw determines the order within that priority group.
The association holds a draw once each quarter when a plot is available.
The date an application was received does not determine draw order.
Unsuccessful applications remain on the list for the next draw.
The association cannot give an applicant a guaranteed waiting time.

forbidden_additions: First-come priority, a guaranteed quarterly vacancy, or a promised waiting time.
A requirement to reapply after every unsuccessful draw.
An invented legal entitlement or a claim that the process has been independently audited.
preserve: Eligibility priority separated from random order within the priority group.
A quarterly opportunity conditional on a vacancy, not a guaranteed offer.
